proportionality.label: Proportionality & Do Not Harm
proportionality.description: AI systems should be proportionate to the problem and not cause disproportionate harm.

fairness.label: Fairness & Non-discrimination
fairness.description: AI systems should not perpetuate discrimination or unfair treatment of individuals or groups.

transparency.label: Transparency & Explainability
transparency.description: AI systems should be transparent, explainable, and auditable.

reproducibility.label: Reproducibility & Accountability
reproducibility.description: AI systems should be reproducible, well-documented, and have clear accountability.

safety.label: Safety & Security
safety.description: AI systems should be robust, secure, and resilient to failures.

awareness.label: Awareness & Literacy
awareness.description: Stakeholders should understand AI capabilities, limitations, and appropriate use.

collaboration.label: Multi-stakeholder Collaboration
collaboration.description: AI development should involve diverse stakeholders throughout the lifecycle.

sustainability.label: Sustainability
sustainability.description: AI systems should consider environmental and long-term societal sustainability.

pre_to_in.rationale: Poor data quality and representativeness makes fairness evaluation more critical during model training. Data cascades compound downstream.
pre_to_in.citation: Sambasivan et al., 'Everyone wants to do the model work, not the data work: Data Cascades in High-Stakes AI', CHI 2021

pre_to_in.rationale: Historical bias in data is amplified during training. Models exacerbate existing data biases rather than merely reflecting them, with bias amplification factors consistently above 1.0.
pre_to_in.citation: Zhao et al., 'Men Also Like Shopping: Reducing Gender Bias Amplification using Corpus-level Constraints', EMNLP 2017

pre_to_in.rationale: Underrepresentation in training data can reduce model accuracy by 15-30% for affected groups. Split representativeness becomes critical when source data is unbalanced.
pre_to_in.citation: Multiple studies on bias amplification factor; EU AI Act Article 10 on training data representativeness

pre_to_in.rationale: Inadequate data governance and privacy practices require enhanced model documentation to maintain accountability and audit trails.
pre_to_in.citation: EU AI Act Article 10 (data governance); ISO/IEC 42001 §8.4 (documentation requirements)

pre_to_in.rationale: Labeling noise and inconsistency cascade into spurious feature reliance during training. Models trained on noisy labels are more likely to learn shortcuts rather than meaningful patterns.
pre_to_in.citation: Sambasivan et al., CHI 2021; Northcutt et al., 'Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets Destabilize Machine Learning Benchmarks', NeurIPS 2021

pre_to_in.rationale: If the appropriateness of AI as a solution was not evaluated, baseline comparison against simpler methods becomes critical to justify model complexity.
pre_to_in.citation: NIST AI RMF Govern 1.2 (proportionality); UNESCO AI Ethics Recommendation §22 (proportionality principle)

in_to_post.rationale: Models with identified algorithmic discrimination require enhanced post-deployment fairness monitoring to detect and mitigate disparate impact in production.
in_to_post.citation: EU AI Act Article 72 (post-market monitoring); NIST AI RMF Measure 2.5 (bias testing)

in_to_post.rationale: Unexplainable models require stronger user-facing transparency controls and communication to maintain trust and enable meaningful human oversight.
in_to_post.citation: UNESCO AI Ethics Recommendation §25 (transparency); EU AI Act Article 13 (transparency obligations)

in_to_post.rationale: Non-robust models have higher deployment failure rates and require enhanced incident response planning and security monitoring in production.
in_to_post.citation: NIST AI RMF Measure 2.6 (robustness assessment); ISO/IEC 42001 §9.1 (monitoring)

in_to_post.rationale: Poor reproducibility during development makes post-deployment auditing and version-controlled retraining critical for maintaining accountability.
in_to_post.citation: ISO/IEC 42001 §8.4 (AI system lifecycle processes); NIST AI RMF Govern 1.4 (documentation)

pre_to_post.rationale: Population bias that persists through training creates feedback loops in production. Post-deployment monitoring must compensate with ongoing fairness checks and redress mechanisms.
pre_to_post.citation: Multiple studies on feedback loops in ML systems; EU AI Act Article 72 (ongoing compliance)

pre_to_post.rationale: Privacy gaps identified during data collection require enhanced security monitoring in production to protect against data breaches and misuse.
pre_to_post.citation: EU AI Act Article 15 (accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity); GDPR Article 25 (data protection by design)

conditionalQuestions.rationale: If protected groups were not assessed during pre-processing, post-deployment monitoring must compensate with disaggregated performance tracking.
conditionalQuestions.citation: EU AI Act Article 9 (risk management); UNESCO AI Ethics §37 (non-discrimination)

conditionalQuestions.rationale: Teams with limited perspective diversity benefit from external review mechanisms post-deployment to catch blind spots in monitoring.
conditionalQuestions.citation: UNESCO AI Ethics Recommendation §38 (multi-stakeholder governance); NIST AI RMF Govern 3 (diverse perspectives)

conditionalQuestions.rationale: Models deployed without explainability methods need runtime explanation capabilities to enable meaningful human oversight.
conditionalQuestions.citation: EU AI Act Article 13 (transparency); NIST AI RMF Measure 2.7 (explainability)

conditionalQuestions.rationale: Untested model robustness requires production-level anomaly detection and automated failsafe mechanisms to prevent harmful outputs.
conditionalQuestions.citation: NIST AI RMF Measure 2.6 (AI system robustness); EU AI Act Article 15 (accuracy and robustness)

conditionalQuestions.rationale: If data representativeness was not audited during pre-processing, model evaluation must explicitly test for representation gaps across demographic subgroups.
conditionalQuestions.citation: Raji et al. (2020) SMACTR framework; Suresh & Guttag (2021) representation bias propagation

conditionalQuestions.rationale: If data quality checks were absent during pre-processing, training-phase sensitivity analysis becomes critical to detect cascading quality issues before deployment.
conditionalQuestions.citation: Sambasivan et al. (2021) data cascades; Northcutt et al. (2021) label error impacts on benchmarks
